A record number of Americans are on the move this weekend — and the trip costs more than it did a year ago.

AAA expects 81.5 million people to travel at least 50 miles for Thanksgiving 2026. That's a slight dip from last year's 81.8 million, ending a three-year streak of records. Nearly 9 in 10 of them are driving.

Here's the money part. Gas has fallen well off its 2026 peak, but it's still higher than it was a year ago — so a full tank for the drive home costs more than last Thanksgiving. Flyers feel it too: AAA puts the average holiday airfare near $800.

My take: the headline is "record travel," but the real story is the quiet math underneath it — paying more to cover the same miles. That's the first thing that nudges a record streak into a dip.

Driving or flying this year, what did the trip actually cost you? 👇
